Most meat has traditionally come from fishing, although as the farming industry becomes more industrialised cattle and livestock are becoming more common. Only in recent times have the populations of fish been carefully monitored, however, meaning some species are rarer than others.

Traditional dishes feature heavily on fruits and vegetables, including olives and nuts exclusive to the Coronite isles. It is hard to pinpoint exactly what a traditional meal would contain, as the availability of fruts, vegetables and grains would vary throughout the year, but most likely any meat invovled would be heavily grilled.
How do ceremonies dedicated to Zhol go? What do they do to show their devotion?

The most traditional form of whorship comes in the form of a mass every saturday, between 9am and 11am, during which they utter prayers and teach about old tales. The tales are not exclusively about Zhol, but rather about the actions of people in the past that did great or selfless deeds to help strengthen the island community.

They also take special note of the summer and winter solstices; both days are vacation days, and during the middle point of the daylight hours a special prayer is held.
